issues.description: revoke_error exposed to API callers without sanitization or access gating
issues.detail: The PR author themselves flags this in the description. RevokeErr is whatever string the backend stuffed in there — could include downstream URLs, hostnames, credential fragments from error wrapping. Either document the threat model and require an explicit capability, or strip it to a boolean/coarse status. Don't ship a field whose own author asks 'is this safe?' in the PR body.

issues.description: FetchLeaseInfo rename is a gratuitous API break with no deprecation
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming it forces every out-of-tree consumer to patch. The honest fix is to keep FetchLeaseTimes as a thin wrapper (or just leave the name — the function now returns more than times, fine, the name is slightly stale, who cares) and add the new fields. Renaming buys nothing here.

issues.description: Two unrelated changes in one patch: feature addition plus a test context swap
issues.detail: The diff adds path/namespace/revoke_error to lease lookup AND swaps namespace.RootContext(nil) for namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) in one test. That context change is unrelated, undocumented, and inconsistent — the other touched test still passes nil. Either fix it everywhere as its own patch or leave it alone. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new fields is one assertion on path; namespace_path and revoke_error are untested
issues.detail: logical_system_test adds a single check that path == 'secret/foo'. namespace_path (the whole point for multi-tenant users) and revoke_error get zero assertions. If these fields matter enough to ship in the API schema, they matter enough to have a test that fails when they regress. Prose in the PR description is not a regression suite.

issues.description: Schema marks `path` Required:true but old clients and old leases may legitimately have empty path
issues.detail: Required:true on a newly-added response field is a compatibility claim the code doesn't actually enforce — leaseInfo.Path is whatever was stored, and historical entries may be empty. Either drop Required, or assert non-empty in code. Pick one; don't lie in the schema.

issues.description: namespace_path omitted when empty but path is always emitted — inconsistent shape
issues.detail: Response conditionally includes namespace_path and revoke_error but unconditionally includes path (even when empty). Pick a convention. Either always-present-with-zero-value or omit-when-empty across all three new fields. Mixed conventions in one response object are how clients grow special cases.

review.summary: Small patch, mostly does what it says, and the rename plumbing is mechanical and correct. Two real problems: (1) the author shipped a field — revoke_error — while openly asking in the PR description whether it's safe to expose; that question gets answered before merge, not after. (2) FetchLeaseTimes is renamed to FetchLeaseInfo with no shim, breaking out-of-tree consumers for cosmetic reasons. Test coverage for the new fields is thin — one assertion on path, nothing on namespace_path or revoke_error. The unrelated t.Context() swap in one test belongs in its own patch. NEEDS-WORK: answer the security question, keep the old method name as a wrapper, add tests for namespace_path and revoke_error, and split the context change out.
